svg.title: SQL self-join for mutual follows — query flow
svg.desc: Five-stage flowchart: the connections table splits into alias a and alias b, which join on reversed follower/followee ids, filtered by follower_id less than followee_id, outputting mutual connection pairs with both dates.

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What does alias a represent in this SQL self-join?')
sendPrompt('What does alias b represent in this SQL self-join?')
sendPrompt('Explain in detail how the bidirectional JOIN condition works for finding mutual follows')
g.text: row (1→5) in a ↔ row (5→1) in b → mutual follow confirmed

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Why does WHERE a.follower_id < a.followee_id prevent duplicate pairs in the output?')
g.text: each mutual pair appears exactly once in the output

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What does the final result set look like for the mutual follows self-join query?')
g.text: user_1 | user_2 | user1→user2 date | user2→user1 date
ordered by user_1, user_2 · first 15 rows (LIMIT 15)
